parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: The expression to evaluate — typically a measure or aggregation like SUM(), COUNT(), or AVERAGE().
parameters.examNote: Must return a scalar value. Cannot be a raw column reference like Sales[Amount].

parameters.name: filter1, filter2, ...
parameters.description: Filters applied to the evaluation context. Each filter modifies or replaces the existing filter context.
parameters.examNote: Accepts ALL(), FILTER(), KEEPFILTERS(), or simple boolean expressions like Sales[Region] = "East".

summary: CALCULATE evaluates an expression under a modified filter context. It is the cornerstone of DAX — nearly every advanced measure uses it directly or indirectly.

examples.label: Filter to one region
examples.explanation: CALCULATE filters Sales to Region = East rows only, then sums their Amount. Row 1 (400) + Row 3 (200) = 600.

examples.label: Remove all filters with ALL()
examples.explanation: ALL(Sales) removes every existing filter on the Sales table. The result is always the full grand total regardless of slicers or visual filters.

steps: Current filter context enters (e.g., slicer: Region = North)
CALCULATE removes or overrides the filter for the specified columns
CALCULATE applies its own filter arguments to the context
The expression is evaluated inside this modified filter context

commonTraps: Boolean filter arguments completely replace the existing column filter — use KEEPFILTERS() to intersect instead of override
CALCULATE inside an iterator (SUMX, AVERAGEX) performs context transition, converting row context into an equivalent filter context
The first argument must be a scalar expression — passing a column reference like Sales[Amount] directly causes an error

sqlEquivalent.expression: SELECT SUM(Amount) FROM Sales WHERE Region = 'East'
sqlEquivalent.note: SQL uses a WHERE clause to filter rows before aggregation. CALCULATE modifies an already-active filter context at runtime — it can override or stack on top of filters applied by slicers and visuals, which has no direct SQL analog.
